cards.text: Picture it, friend: the LORD speaks to Joshua, Israel's leader, and tells him to have the Israelites designate the cities of refuge. And this isn't a brand-new idea. God already gave these instructions once, through someone else.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua He already gave the instructions for the cities of refuge through ___.

cards.text: Here's the setup. Somebody's going to need to RUN, with the avenger of blood behind him, and God says these cities are his refuge.

cards.question: Who does God say can flee to a city of refuge?

answers.text: Someone who kills another by accident
Someone who steals from a neighbor

cards.text: So he runs, and he makes it to the entrance of one city's gate. I'm a stamper who hops on a gold base, friend, so if anybody chased ME, I'd arrive sometime next Tuesday.

cards.question: Standing at the entrance of the city gate, the man states his case before the city's ___.
After the man states his case at the city gate, the elders make him camp outside the walls.

cards.text: But hold on. What if the avenger of blood comes chasing him all the way to that city?

cards.question: When the avenger of blood pursues the man to the city of refuge, the elders must not hand him over.
Why must the elders protect the man from the avenger of blood?

answers.text: He killed his neighbor with no prior malice
He already paid a fine to the family
He was born inside that city

cards.text: He's inside now. But this is NOT a quick stop, like ducking under an awning till the rain quits.

cards.question: How long does the man have to stay in the city of refuge?

answers.text: Until his trial and the high priest's death
Until the avenger of blood gives up
Until seven full years have passed

cards.question: Even after the high priest serving at that time dies, the man has to stay in the city of refuge for the rest of his life.

cards.text: So they set apart three cities in the hill country: Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem and Hebron. Then three more beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho: Bezer, Ramoth in Gilead and Golan in Bashan.
Then the passage spells out exactly who these cities are for. And the list is WIDER than you might expect.

cards.question: The cities of refuge are for all the Israelites and the ___ among them.
As the passage wraps up, what does it say the cities of refuge are for?

answers.text: So the manslayer isn't killed before his trial
So the tribes have safe places to trade
So the priests have more land to farm
